entities.summary: José María Rojas Garrido was a Colombian Senator, and statesmen, who as the first Presidential Designate became Acting President of the United States of Colombia in 1866 during the absence of President elect Tomás Cipriano de Mosquera. He was a prominent journalist for several Liberal Party newspapers, and is considered one of the most important orators in Colombia's history.

entities.name: José María Rojas Garrido
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
José María Rojas Garrido (1824–1883) emerged as a pivotal figure in mid-19th century Colombian politics, serving as the first Presidential Designate and briefly as Acting President of the United States of Colombia in 1866. Born in El Agrado, Huila, on June 7, 1824, his career spanned law, journalism, and statesmanship, placing him at the heart of the Liberal Party's ideological struggles during a period of intense federalist experimentation and civil strife across the nascent South American republics. His brief presidential tenure, though overshadowed by the more dominant figure of Tomás Cipriano de Mosquera, marked a critical constitutional precedent for presidential succession in the newly formed United States of Colombia, establishing a mechanism for leadership continuity in the absence of an elected head of state.

Rojas Garrido's political ascent was built upon a formidable reputation as an orator and a prolific journalist, talents he honed in various Liberal Party newspapers, including *El Tiempo* and *La América*. Beyond his journalistic contributions, he held multiple ministerial portfolios, including Secretary of the Interior and Foreign Relations, and served as a Senator for several terms, demonstrating a consistent commitment to federalist principles and liberal reforms. His most notable governmental role came in 1866 when, as the first Presidential Designate, he assumed the acting presidency from April 1 to May 22, during Tomás Cipriano de Mosquera's absence from the capital. This temporary leadership, while brief, was a direct application of the 1863 Rionegro Constitution's provisions for presidential succession, a foundational document he himself helped shape.
